state:
- Novelty is thin: teriflunomide is the canonical pick given S4 (essentially the only approved DHODH inhibitor), and differentiation-by-DHODH-inhibition is an established AML direction, so the mechanism is borrowed rather than new; the answer's own admission that prior AML evaluation of leflunomide/teriflunomide 'would need checking' leaves the novelty claim untested. Fix: verify prior DHODH-inhibitor AML literature (brequinar, leflunomide/teriflunomide, clinical DHODH programs) and foreground the genuinely new elements — the uridine-discriminated OXPHOS/residual-disease bridge B2 applied after cytarabine (S2 context) — instead of the S4 mechanism itself.
- B1, the pivotal bridge, is unquantified: the hypothesis's go/no-go gate is 'differentiation at concentrations achievable from approved dosing,' yet no numbers anchor it, and teriflunomide's >99% protein binding (recalled in the answer as unverified) predicts a small free fraction versus putative AML-active concentrations. Fix: anchor the ranking with the recalled steady-state exposure and free fraction from the FDA label against a differentiation-inducing EC50 from S4-type systems, explicitly labeling both as to-be-verified, before assigning promisingness 0.55.
- One pharmacodynamic readout is misaligned with DHODH pharmacology: dUMP accumulation is indirect and confoundable, whereas direct on-target DHODH blockade is evidenced by upstream accumulation of dihydroorotate/N-carbamoylaspartate with depletion of downstream uridine/pyrimidine pools, as measured in S4. Fix: make those upstream/downstream metabolite-pool changes the primary on-target test, with uridine-rescue of both metabolic and differentiation phenotypes retained as the falsifier.
